title: Multiplexed scorer scheduling and per-request token governor to reduce rerank tail latency
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Goal: reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for the reranking endpoint by combining a multiplexed scorer scheduling strategy with a per-request token governor and soft timeouts. This ticket implements a runtime scheduler that shards incoming candidate scoring across a configurable number of scorer lanes, enforces a per-request token budget to limit worst-case compute, and introduces a polite soft-timeout path that returns a best-effort partial ranking when deadlines are missed. The design aims to preserve top-k quality for common cases while bounding tail latency for bursty traffic and very long candidate lists.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for 1k-candidate rerank workload <= 350ms on target dedicated machines (p95 measured over 30m window)
99th percentile latency reduced by at least 30% compared to baseline for same QPS
end-to-end correctness: final top-10 overlap >= 0.95 with baseline model on benchmark prompt set when no token governor trimming is applied
Operational: metrics emitted for lane utilization, token-governor rejections, soft-timeout occurrences, and fallback paths
Config: scheduler lane-count and per-request token-budget adjustable via model-route config and effective immediately without restart
tasks: Prototype multiplexed lane scheduler in inference runtime (C++): queueing + round-robin windowing
Add token-governor middleware in request pipeline (Go): measure token budget, preempt or trim inputs
Integrate soft-timeout handler that produces best-effort partial ranking using early-exit scorer
Add metrics (Prometheus) and tracing spans for scheduling decisions and budget enforcement
Run A/B perf comparison on dedicated cluster, collect p50/p95/p99 and correctness metrics
comments: 2026-03-10 Diego Martinez: Initial writeup — sketched scheduler API and token-governor semantics. Decided to prefer cooperative preemption (trim candidate lists) over outright request rejection for better UX.
